vulnerable_statements.reason: The function walks every child dentry of the directory in one pass while holding inode->i_lock and alias->d_lock, and it never stops to reschedule. A directory can collect millions of child dentries (for example, many cached lookups). Adding or removing a watch, which an unprivileged user can do with inotify/fanotify, then holds the spinlocks for a long, unbounded time. That causes soft or hard lockups and stalls other CPUs waiting on these locks, so it is a denial of service.

Each child's d_lock is taken inside the unbounded loop, still under the parent's i_lock and d_lock. This adds lock contention across all CPUs and makes the long time spent in the critical section worse.

suggested_fix: Do not update every child's flags eagerly while holding the spinlocks. Set or clear DCACHE_FSNOTIFY_PARENT_WATCHED only when the parent's watch state changes to 'watched'. When a watch is removed, mark the parent so the stale flag is cleared lazily: when a child next reports an event (__fsnotify_parent), it sees that the parent no longer watches children and clears its own flag. Another option is to bound the work, for example by dropping the locks and calling cond_resched() during the walk with a cursor, so the time spent holding a spinlock is no longer proportional to the number of children.
